title: 4-round AES-192: ten-constant distinguisher, sixteen inputs

target.description: AES-192 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 4 rounds. The collision is between internal byte-valued functions under the same unknown round keys, not between two AES master keys. Four consecutive inner rounds include MixColumns in every round, under any fixed unknown round-key values. This component applies to each AES key length but is not a prefix-cipher key-recovery result.

setting.key_relation: Four fixed, unknown 128-bit round keys. The structural argument does not use their master-key dependencies, and therefore also applies to keys derived from any of the standard AES key lengths.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: Fix c and the other twelve input bytes; vary y over N distinct values, where N<=256. The selected concrete endpoint uses N=16; the source does not claim a uniform advantage for every smaller N.
assumptions: The source describes right-going ShiftRow. Standard AES uses left-going shifts. Reindexing columns by J(r,c)=(r,-c mod 4) conjugates the independent-round-key construction; inputs, outputs and recovered round keys are reflected consistently before standard key expansion. This coordinate normalization is a local structural interpretation, not a complete attack reproduction.
Enumerate ten unknown byte constants describing the partial function. The paper calls N=16 sufficient in practice but supplies no numerical distinguishing advantage or proof for all N.
setting.reference_model: Chosen-input access to four fixed-key inner rounds is compared with a uniformly random permutation on 128-bit blocks, using the same input structures and projected output tests.

time.note: The source prices 2^80 parameter guesses times N observations in unspecified elementary operations. The N=16 exponent is an algebraic substitution, not a conversion to AES encryptions.

data.note: The text gives a parameter family and separately identifies N=16 as sufficient; no success guarantee is assigned to every small N.

memory.note: No complete peak-storage budget is stated.

preprocessing.note: The paper does not separately price setup for this endpoint.

success.description: Derived ideal-permutation distinguishing-advantage bound for the complete ten-byte constant-enumeration test, with one fixed c triplet, other fixed input bytes, and N distinct preselected active-byte values, 1<=N<=256. Property4 determines the observed nonzero rank8 output projection by at most2^80 constant choices, fixed independently of the oracle. The actual AES constants are included, so AES acceptance is one. For a uniform128-bit permutation a fixed ordered projected signature has probability at most2^(-8N)*product(j=0..N-1)(1-j/2^128)^-1. The product is less than2 for this domain; union over all constants gives false-positive probability at most min(1,2^(81-8N)). Thus Adv>=max(0,1-2^(81-8N)), and N=16 gives Adv>=1-2^-47. The bound is vacuous for N<=10 and positive for N>=11. Neither independent guesses, iid output bytes, birthday acquisition nor key recovery is assumed. This is a new conservative counting inference, not an author-printed advantage; native operation counts and unknown costs are unchanged.

components.description: Chapter6–7 Property4: complete enumeration of all ten unknown byte constants contains the actual values for this fixed unknown key, so the genuine function has a matching signature for every sampled y. This is one-sided AES acceptance; it neither bounds wrong signatures nor gives a total distinguishing advantage.

review.scope: Verified exact source experiment, deterministic AES acceptance, ideal-permutation sampling without replacement and conservative whole-decision bound. Independently source-first and endpoint reviewed. This does not certify unknown resources, disputed source claims, attack reproduction or a new full-paper audit.

evidence.interpretation: No numerical distinguishing advantage is stated for the fixed N=16 exhaustive ten-byte constant test. Actual-constant coverage makes AES acceptance deterministic, but the source does not give an ideal-permutation whole-search false-positive rate. Six key-only bytes and four c-dependent bytes are enumerated constants, not a master-key recovery output. Do not invent2^(80-8N) as an exact permutation bound or transfer birthday acquisition to this different test.
